statement: Report estimates 1.5°C warming since the 1950s and rainfall decline from 85 mm (1950) to 63 mm (2020); June 2020-November 2022 drought affected up to one-third of people and worsened food insecurity.
compact_statement: Report estimates 1.5°C warming since the 1950s and rainfall decline from 85 mm (1950) to 63 mm (2020); June 2020-November 2022 drought affected up to one-third of people and worsened food insecurity.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, section A, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 65), climate trends and drought effects.

uncertainty: Up-to-one-third estimate; no regional breakdown here.

statement: The report states that floods occur nearly once every two years, have destroyed villages and livestock, and on several occasions disrupted at least 10,000 livelihoods and caused about 10 deaths.
compact_statement: The report states that floods occur nearly once every two years, have destroyed villages and livestock, and on several occasions disrupted at least 10,000 livelihoods and caused about 10 deaths.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, section A, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 65), flood impacts.

uncertainty: The cited passage does not identify locations or dates for the individual flood events.

statement: World Bank modeling in the report estimates climate-related GDP losses of 9.3% by 2050 under its dry/pessimistic scenario without adaptation, compared with 5.7% with partial adaptation.
compact_statement: World Bank modeling in the report estimates climate-related GDP losses of 9.3% by 2050 under its dry/pessimistic scenario without adaptation, compared with 5.7% with partial adaptation.
scenario: Dry/pessimistic climate scenario; no adaptation compared with selected partial adaptation measures.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4, printed pp. 26-27 and 60 (PDF pp. 33-34, 67), climate macroeconomic scenario summary and adaptation comparison.

uncertainty: Model result aggregates selected impact channels; it is not an observed GDP loss.

statement: The G5 CCDR projects that under medium growth and its dry/pessimistic climate scenario without adaptation, Mauritania’s poverty rate in 2050 would be 0.2 percentage points above the no-climate baseline.
compact_statement: The G5 CCDR projects that under medium growth and its dry/pessimistic climate scenario without adaptation, Mauritania’s poverty rate in 2050 would be 0.2 percentage points above the no-climate baseline.
scenario: Medium-growth baseline with dry/pessimistic climate scenario; no adaptation.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.1.6, printed p. 73 (PDF p. 73), modeled poverty impact under climate scenarios.

uncertainty: The reported change is relative to the no-climate baseline and uses 2017 household-survey data in a macro-microsimulation.
